Over 355 earthquakes hit Iran in a month
TEHRAN – A total of 356 earthquakes have been recorded across the country in a week from September 23 to October 22, according to the seismological networks of the Institute of Geophysics of the University of Tehran.
Statistically, 322 earthquakes with magnitudes smaller than 3, 30 earthquakes with a magnitude between 3 and 4, and four earthquakes with a magnitude between 4 and 5 have occurred in the country, irsc reported.
Of the total quakes, two had a magnitude of 4.2 on the Richter scale which occurred on October 16 and 20 in Kerman province.
Among the provinces of the country, Khorasan Razavi experienced the highest number of earthquakes with 44, followed by Kerman with 40, and Yazd with 30 earthquakes.
During the same period, 10 earthquakes hit Tehran, the biggest one had a magnitude of 3.3 on the Richter scale.
A total of 2,380 earthquakes with a magnitude of more than 2.5 on the Richter scale were recorded across the country over the past calendar year (March 2025–March 2026), according to the Seismological networks of the Institute of Geophysics of the University of Tehran, Mehr news agency reported.
Out of recorded earthquakes, 910 had a magnitude greater than 3, 130 had a magnitude greater than 4, and 15 had a magnitude greater than 5 on the Richter scale.
The Iranian plateau is located in a very seismically active region of the world and is known not only for its major catastrophic earthquakes but also for the disasters relating to natural hazards, especially earthquakes.
About 2 percent of the earthquakes in the world occur in Iran, but more than 6 percent of the victims of the world’s earthquakes during the 20th century are reported from Iranian earthquakes.

Stone-covered roof provides "absolute camouflage" for Gamaya Farms eco-resort in India

Unknown Publisher

Stone-covered roof provides “absolute camouflage” for Gamaya Farms eco-resort in India
Architecture studio Biome Environmental Solutions has used a hill-like roof covered in local stone and walls of compressed earth bricks to conceal this eco-resort within its site in India.
Named Gamaya Farms, the resort is located in the town of Vikarabad, near Hyderabad and has a total built area of 854 square metres.
It comprises a series of individual guesthouses and farm plots organised around a shared amenities block at its centre.
Biome Environmental Solutions designed each building to offer a different spatial experience of the surrounding landscape, from the hill-like vaulted roof of the central pavilion to a mixture of elevated and subterranean guesthouses.
“Gamaya Farms redefines architectural iconism not through bold geometry, but through absolute camouflage and tectonic erasure,” director Anurag Tamhankar told Dezeen.
“Rather than treating the program as a monolithic footprint, the master plan deconstructs the traditional resort layout into distinct, site-specific architectural typologies,” he added.
“Taking cues from the surrounding hills and forest to create an intervention that transitions out of the ground, the design disperses the program across decentralised pockets of the land, offering distinct sensory experiences.”
The curved, single-storey pavilion at the centre of Gamaya Farms contains the main entrance and reception at its western end. This leads into a large multi-purpose hall and dining room, as well as utility areas and bathrooms.
Large, circular windows set in exposed earth-block walls fill these spaces with light, and are shaded by the vaulted form of the pavilion’s hill-like roof, which extends to shelter a paved terrace to the north.
Punctured by rows of large, arched openings, this roof was constructed using shotcrete, or sprayed concrete, applied over chicken and weld mesh and topped with a layer of unworked local rubble.
In front of the central pavilion, four guesthouses are partially sunken into a slope, with narrow, dark entrance stairs opening out into bedrooms with large, north-facing windows.
Further toward the wooded edges of the site are two Forest Pavilions – cylindrical structures that are perched atop concrete stilts and accessed via spiral staircases in yellow-painted steel.
The lower levels of these guesthouses contain bathrooms lined in smooth, curved plaster, while above, their circular bedrooms are wrapped by glazing and a balcony with yellow-painted railings.
“The subterranean cottages, sunk into the ground, preserve the expansive view from the pavilion, while getting their own private views,” Tamhankar eplained.
“The isolated forest cottages are tucked into the woodland perimeter, with a 360-degree view of the forest canopy,” he added.
Another resort in India recently featured on Dezeen is The Earthen Retreat by AKSH Architects, which comprises a cluster of small abandoned buildings coated in mud and lime plaster, and Serenity by Ma+rs, which is distinguished by its thatched roofs.

Iran-China project to restore wetlands, curb dust storms enters implementation phase
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26

Iran-China project to restore wetlands, curb dust storms enters implementation phase
TEHRAN – A joint Iran-China project to restore Salehiyeh and Allahabad wetlands, located west and southwest of Tehran, and curb dust storm sources has entered the implementation phase, with planned measures covering more than 48,000 hectares.
The wetlands are important ecosystems that help sustain local biodiversity and regulate environmental conditions. However, declining rainfall, drought, excessive water extraction, and drainage projects have contributed to their degradation and the shrinking water bodies.
A specialized webinar to review the operational aspects of the memorandum of understanding for the joint project was held on Saturday with the participation of University of Tehran faculty members and representatives of relevant organizations.
Coordinated by the Secretariat of the National Dust Storm Headquarters, the project involves the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the University of Tehran, and the Plan and Budget Organization. It aims to curb active dust storm sources, improve the hydrological regimes of the two wetlands, and enhance the livelihoods of local communities.
Under the plan developed for the first phase, rehabilitating drainage systems and reopening waterways, establishing living and non-living windbreaks, implementing biological measures, using environmentally compatible mulches, and empowering local communities have been envisaged, Mehr news agency reported.
According to the Department of Environment (DOE), in accordance with President Masoud Pezeshkian’s directives and to follow up on the resolutions of Iran’s National Headquarters for Dust Storm Policy and Coordination, a specialized webinar was held on Saturday, reviewing the operational aspects of the tripartite memorandum of understanding (MOU) of the Iran-China joint project. Officials from the University of Tehran and other related organizations attended the webinar.
Addressing the event, Behzad Raygani, secretary of the National Secretariat for Sand and Dust Storms, outlined the parameters for joint effort while highlighting the need for integrated water resources management, restoration of wetland ecosystems, development of conservation agriculture, and stabilization of soil in critical dust hotspots.
The initiative serves as an example of national synergy, and proactive environmental diplomacy will be pursued across the short-term, medium-term, and long-term.
Pezeshkian pushes for drafting action plan to combat desertification
In September, President Pezeshkian highlighted the need to draft a five-year Iranian-Chinese action plan to manage airborne dust and combat desertification in line with a memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed by the two countries.
The MOU was inked in the last month of spring in 2025, in Lanzhou, China, to promote scientific cooperation and address sand and dust storms (SDSs) challenges, IRNA reported.
Following specialized meetings and an assessment of scientific and operational indicators, a five-year action plan is scheduled to be developed, and two regions have been designated as pilot sites for implementing joint efforts.
The selected areas include Salehiyeh Wetland, a major dust source affecting Alborz, Qazvin, and Tehran provinces, and Tabas desert, another main dust hotspot in the country, chosen due to their roles in the expansion of desertification, sandstorms, and their impacts on agriculture and infrastructure.
Highlighting the importance of protecting natural resources and the environment, Pezeshkian called for taking action against unauthorized construction and illegal activities that undermine regulations and lead to environmental consequences, as well as benefiting from the capacities and expertise of the Chinese Academy of Sciences in implementing pilot projects.
The official made the remarks in a meeting held on September 13 to give an account of the progress in the bilateral MOU.
Moreover, the president urged the University of Tehran to maintain constant collaboration with the Chinese Academy of Sciences and develop a joint action plan to be assessed and discussed in the next meetings. The official also asked the Plan and Budget Organization to secure funds required for the studies and measures in the five-year action plan.
Dust storms are significant environmental challenges that adversely affect food security, human health, and the sustainable development process at national and regional levels.
Being located in an arid and semi-arid area, Iran has been negatively impacted by climate change. The rise in temperatures, drop in precipitation, intensified droughts, and frequent SDSs have not only threatened the ecosystem and biodiversity but also jeopardized the country’s food security by exacerbating soil erosion, expanding desertification, and declining agricultural productivity.

Galp confirmed that talks with Moeve shareholders to merge downstream operations have collapsed, and says the result will not affect its operations.

The Portuguese oil and gas company stressed, however, that this outcome has no impact on its operations or on confidence in the company.

"After extensive discussions, it was not possible to reach a commercial agreement with Galp. We remain focused on executing our transformation with financial discipline and on generating sustainable long-term value."
The Portuguese online newspaper ECO (source in Portuguese) had reported on Sunday night that the deal had fallen through because Paula Amorim had not agreed to the Spanish company’s demands, according to sources familiar with the talks.
Galp’s downstream business is underpinned by "a leading retail network" in Portugal and by "a significant portfolio of energy transition projects in Sines", the statement adds. Serbia after Vucic: Who will be PM and when will a government be formed?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
11:28:25 UTC
20:28:25 KST

Serbia after Vucic: Who will be PM and when will a government be formed?
Uncertainty remains over key positions after student-led movement deals blow to longtime leader’s political dominance.
A student-led opposition movement has emerged victorious in Serbia’s snap parliamentary election, ending former President Aleksandar Vucic’s long grip on power.
The Student List’s win on Sunday followed nearly two years of youth-led protests triggered by the death of 16 people in a railway station canopy collapse in the city of Novi Sad in 2024.
Demonstrations demanding accountability quickly evolved into a wider political campaign against alleged corruption and capture of democratic institutions. In its electoral programme presented in September, the Student List said fighting corruption and organised crime were among its main priorities. It also pledged to raise living standards, boost employment, improve education, ensure media freedom and the independence of Serbia’s institutions.
After declaring victory on Sunday, the movement also said it would work to improve relations with neighbouring countries following a period of tension during Vucic’s more than decade-long rule.
Here’s what you should know:
What are the latest results?
The Republic Election Commission (RIK) announced on Monday that the Student List had won 52.54 percent of the vote, based on 8,077 processed polling stations out of 8,392.
The figures also showed the United Serbia list, led by Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party, had secured 39.29 percent of ballots cast.
Voter turnout stood at 68.78 percent, a record high in more than 30 years, according to RIK data on Sunday.
What’s next?
While the final election result is not yet known, the figures mean that the Student List will be able to form a majority in Serbia’s 250-seat parliament on its own.
The bloc is projected to win 140 seats, well ahead of the 126 mandates required for a majority, while United Serbia is expected to have 103.
The remaining seats are set to go to the Alliance of Vojvodina Hungarians (three); the Albanian political bloc (two); and the Rasim Ljajc-Ljudski and SDA Sandzak lists, with one each.
Who could be the new prime minister?
Unlike United Serbia, which named Vucic as its candidate for prime minister before the election, the Student List made no such announcement during the campaign.
Since its formal creation, the list has avoided highlighting single candidates, eager to emphasise the collective nature of the movement that brought together academics, doctors and workers.
During the campaign, the movement was led by Ilija Srdanovic, a professor at the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Novi Sad. The cardiologist is now seen as the most likely candidate to become the next prime minister, but it remains unclear who will take over key ministries, including those of internal affairs, finance and justice.
When will the new government be formed?
This depends on when the final election results will be announced and when parliament convenes.
The new National Assembly must be established within 30 days of the final results being announced.
A government must be formed within 90 days after that – but the Student List’s clear majority removes the need for lengthy coalition talks.
What about the president?
Vucic has dominated Serbia’s politics – first as prime minister and then as president – since 2014.
Following his call for the snap parliamentary vote last month and his resignation as president, the post has been held temporarily by Ana Brnabic, the president of the National Assembly.
Brnabic is obliged to call for an extraordinary presidential election which must be held no later than three months after the end of Vucic’s mandate.
Vucic resigned on September 27 , so the deadline to hold a vote is December 27 .
The president of Serbia is elected directly by the citizens, not by the representatives in the assembly, but the post is largely ceremonial.

Pakistani Mustafa Prize laureate explores nanotechnology in fight against breast cancer
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
11:26:45 UTC
20:26:45 KST

Pakistani Mustafa Prize laureate explores nanotechnology in fight against breast cancer
TEHRAN - Nanotechnology is opening new avenues for breast cancer treatment by improving drug delivery, overcoming resistance to chemotherapy, and reducing damage to healthy cells. Pakistani medicinal chemist Muhammad Iqbal Choudhary, a 2021 Mustafa Prize laureate, is among the researchers exploring how advanced drug-delivery systems can make cancer therapies more precise and effective.
Breast cancer remains a major global health challenge, with patients often facing recurrence, drug resistance, and severe treatment-related side effects. Conventional chemotherapy targets rapidly dividing cells but can also damage healthy tissues, including hair follicles, the gastrointestinal lining, and bone marrow. Meanwhile, cancer cells can develop multidrug resistance (MDR) by activating molecular pumps that expel drugs before they can take effect.
“Cancers are very difficult, complex, and diverse diseases,” Choudhary said. He explained that chemotherapy drugs often affect both cancerous and healthy cells, making it challenging to target tumors without causing significant side effects.
Choudhary, who heads the International Center for Chemical and Biological Sciences (ICCBS) at the University of Karachi, serves as vice president of The World Academy of Sciences (TWAS) and coordinates the Standing Committee on Scientific and Technological Cooperation of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (COMSTECH).
Receiving the Mustafa Prize marked a turning point in his scientific career, providing renewed motivation and focus. Since then, his research group has increasingly concentrated on innovative breast cancer treatments and smarter drug-delivery technologies.
Nanocarriers offer one promising approach by encapsulating therapeutic compounds in microscopic particles that protect drugs from premature degradation and release them more effectively at tumor sites. These systems can use passive targeting, which exploits the increased permeability of tumor blood vessels, or active targeting, in which antibodies, peptides, or other molecules help nanoparticles bind to cancer-cell receptors.
According to Choudhary, nanoparticles can contribute both to drug discovery and to delivering existing medicines more precisely, potentially improving their effectiveness while limiting harmful side effects.
One promising strategy involves poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA), a biodegradable and biocompatible polymer widely investigated for controlled drug delivery. Adding vitamin E-derived TPGS may further help counter drug resistance by interfering with the energy-dependent mechanisms that cancer cells use to expel chemotherapy drugs.
Researchers are also investigating nanoparticles coated with natural cell membranes to help them evade immune clearance and accumulate more effectively in tumors. Platelet membranes are particularly promising because their surface proteins may support tumor targeting. A 2025 preclinical study reported greater uptake of platelet-membrane-coated, bufalin-loaded PLGA nanoparticles by tumor cells than that of uncoated particles.
These advances could be particularly valuable against triple-negative breast cancer, an aggressive subtype lacking estrogen, progesterone, and HER2 receptors, which limits conventional targeted treatment options. Nanoparticle-based systems that respond to local tumor conditions may offer alternative ways to deliver drugs without relying on these receptors.
Despite the promise, significant challenges remain. Producing platelet-membrane-coated nanoparticles consistently at clinical scale is difficult, and incomplete membrane coverage remains a concern. Such technologies must overcome manufacturing and regulatory hurdles before routine clinical use becomes possible.
Choudhary emphasizes that, although increasingly selective therapies are available, no drug can yet deliver absolute disease-specific precision. Integrating molecular biology, nanotechnology, and medicinal chemistry could nevertheless bring researchers closer to safer, more effective treatments for cancers that have long resisted conventional therapies.

Koretsky urges business to plan for worst case, warns of $1.5 bln budget gap
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
13:26:04 EET
20:26:04 KST

Prime Minister of Ukraine Serhiy Koretsky has called on the business community to prepare in advance for the most critical scenarios regarding enemy attacks and economic challenges.
"When we talk to founders and top management, I’ve sensed a certain attitude that 'it will somehow blow over.' Perhaps I won't be targeted by missiles or drones, perhaps my sector won't be touched. Therefore, first: I would strongly ask and recommend thinking according to the most critical scenario of events. Thinking ahead about alternative production sites: who you can cooperate with, where you can make a private label if we are talking about consumer goods, if your enterprise is hit. How to talk in advance with suppliers, perhaps even for imported goods, how to conclude framework contracts and be ready rather than doing it all later. Looking at alternative premises for relocation, for restoration. In other words, think in the most critical scenario. It is better to be ready for this and have it not happen than to find oneself in an unexpected situation," Koretsky said at the 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF) themed "People. Business. Economy. What's Next?" in Kyiv on Monday, as reported by an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent.
According to the Prime Minister, enemy strikes have already caused over $7.7 billion in losses, with more than 1 million square meters of various types of real estate, both state and private, destroyed or damaged. Significant destruction has hit energy, metallurgy, logistics, processing enterprises, retail, and other sectors.
"Considering these losses, considering the strikes, we already see that by the end of the year the state budget will underfulfill its plans and forecasts by about $1.5 billion. That is the baseline forecast we have today," he stated.
At the same time, he emphasized that despite all this, the country's economy continues to function.
"If we think in terms of PnL (Profit and Loss statement), allocating a lot of funds to support business is impossible. There is no such PnL, because we can only cover one-third of the budget. Even realizing, clearly realizing this, we live even on a cash flow principle and in a certain way go all-in, allocating certain funds to support programs, to various subsidies, to grant programs. Because we realize that without this support, business – small, medium, and large in particular – cannot be sufficiently resilient to counter enemy attacks. And this is the conscious logic and tactics of the government," Koretsky noted.
The Prime Minister stressed that the government will continue programs that have proven their effectiveness, notably the "Affordable Loans 5-7-9%" program. He noted that since the program's inception, UAH 580 billion has been issued, with the current loan portfolio principal standing at around UAH 200 billion. He recalled the recent decision allowing large businesses to receive about UAH 2 billion "in one hand per group of companies" at a preferential interest rate of around 10%.
"The 2026 budget allocated Hr 18 billion. We are expanding this program and see that by the end of the year it will be Hr 22 billion. We currently have a certain deficit on four billion, but one way or another we will cover it, because we consider this to be one of the fundamentally important, correct programs that genuinely supports business," the Prime Minister said.
He also pointed out the necessity of establishing a war risk insurance and damage compensation system. Koretsky recalled the proposal to create a special fund in the budget with an initial state contribution of $1 billion, which partners would double or triple.
"How will this work further? A simplified procedure. Compensation within 30 days after processing. And the tariff for this insurance risk must be very basic, symbolic, we are aiming at approximately 2%. And the maximum damage compensation will be about $5 million in one hand," the Prime Minister detailed.
Koretsky also stated that there is currently no consensus or support for increasing the Value Added Tax (VAT) from 20% to 21% to fund this special fund.
"There is no consensus among big and medium business, there is no support in parliament yet. We are looking for other mechanisms, we will see how the budgetary process proceeds in parliament and build from that. But we have no other path, we must find the instrument. Together we will see what we can contribute," Koretsky emphasized.

Details
If consultation is to be undertaken on an amendment to the regulations or the implementation of new regulation, the MAA will issue an NPA. The NPA will explain the rationale behind the amendment, the possible impact on the regulated community (developed into an impact assessment (IA)) and set the deadline for comment/feedback. Feedback is important to further develop the IA.
Comments or enquiries on any NPA are to be sent to DSA-MAA-MRPEnquiries@mod.gov.uk by the date stated in the NPA. Please use the NPA Response Form template provided below to return your consolidated comments.
After the comments closure date, the NPA will be removed from the website.
NPA comment response sheets contain the collated MAA responses to individual NPA publications.
In the final preparation for publication similar Regulated Community comments have been consolidated into one response.
Some of the MAA responses to the Regulated Community comments may have been superseded by further internal review prior to the official publication of the new issue.

British premier says revising UK’s Brexit deal with EU could ‘bring people together’
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
11:22:23 UTC
20:22:23 KST

Aysu Bicer
26 October 2026•Update: 26 October 2026
British Premier Andy Burnham has said that revising the UK’s relationship with the EU could help bring people together, while insisting that any decision to rejoin the bloc would be for the British public to make.
Speaking in an interview on Monday on ITV’s Good Morning Britain, hosted by Susanna Reid and Richard Madeley, Burnham said he would like to see the UK rejoin the EU in his lifetime but stressed that he would not impose his personal views on the public.
“I’ve said – I’m going to be honest – in my lifetime I would like to see that happen, but I am not going to move ahead of the public. I am not going to dictate in terms of my own opinions here. You have to make sure that the British public are the bosses here,” he said.
Asked whether he saw himself as the prime minister destined to take Britain back into the EU, Burnham replied: “Honestly, I don’t.”
He said his priority was to take a pragmatic approach to the country’s challenges, adding: “I see it as my job to be pragmatic about the whole situation. Can I make it work better? Can I add growth to the British economy?”
Burnham rejected suggestions that he was reopening the Brexit referendum debate in breach of a promise made during the Makerfield by-election campaign.
Instead, he reiterated his argument that the UK should reconsider its post-Brexit arrangements with the EU, saying the current settlement was not working.
He also argued that a more practical and open discussion about Brexit could help bridge political and social divisions that have persisted since the 2016 referendum.
“And [to] go back to Brexit, by just talking about it in a more practical way, by being honest about it … that can start to bring people together who voted in different ways,” he said.
“The divides that we’ve lived through in the last decade really do need to end, and we need to pull people together …”
Burnham said addressing the UK’s relationship with Europe was necessary to provide the country with a clear direction.
“I’m trying to give the country a direction and there is no way I can do that without coming back to the relationship with Europe and saying, ‘Look, here are some options as to how we got this right.’”
He again ruled out seeking to rejoin the EU before the next general election.
 
Rules out early election
During the interview, Burnham also dismissed speculation about an early general election, saying there would be no election “anytime soon.”
Asked whether he was preparing the public for an early election, he replied: “No, I’ve ruled that out.”
Pressed on whether that was definite, Burnham said he had made his position clear before the Labour Party conference.
“I just don’t think people want another backward-looking squabble. I think they want me to get on with the job,” he said.
Reid returned to the issue towards the end of the interview, prompting Burnham to reiterate that an early election was not on his agenda.
“My mind is not on that [an early election]. I don’t know if that is coming over here, but it genuinely is not on that. There is no election coming anytime soon. People may as well just put that out of their mind,” he said.

Agricultural Year Recap and Spring Planting Scenarios: UCAB to Host #DoAgro26 Conference
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
13:22:21 EET
20:22:21 KST

On December 4, the 18th International Conference “Agribusiness in Ukraine” (#DoAgro26) will take place in Truskavets (Lviv Oblast). The event will be attended by government officials, market leaders, and leading agricultural producers.
This was reported by the press service of the organizers—the “Ukrainian Agribusiness Club” and the UCABevent agency.
This year, the event is completely revamping its format and usual location to take stock of the past year and develop a roadmap for the upcoming season.
This isn’t about monologues or dry reports—those are a thing of the past. What lies ahead is the search for new operating models: open dialogue with government officials, collective brainstorming, and making strategic decisions right here and now. The main goal is to find effective operating models under the new rules of the game.
Participating in #DoAgro26 means:
- Pre-conference fireside chat: an evening meeting with a guest expert, an informal conversation, and quality networking on the eve of the conference.
- Open agropolitical debates: no imposed topics or pre-written scripts. Participants themselves choose the direction of the discussion and the most pressing issues right here and now.
- Collective brainstorming and roundtables: a format where everyone becomes a co-creator of the event, joins the discussions, and collaboratively shapes effective strategies.
- Direct access to solutions: the opportunity for open dialogue with government officials and market leaders.
The program will focus on key issues:
- 2026 in Review: How the agribusiness market (did NOT) adapt to challenges.
- Checkmate to the season’s challenges: scenarios for the 2027 spring planting season and strategic moves for agribusiness.
- A macroeconomic overview above and below the line—from global trends to the financial realities of agribusiness.
The “Agribusiness in Ukraine” conference will be held in cooperation with the International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, and in partnership with the Ministry of Finance of the Czech Republic. Valtra, part of AGCO Corporation, is the exclusive technical partner, and Credit Agricole is the gold financial partner.
Agricultural producers and participants in previous UCAAB events are eligible for a 20% discount off the base price, while association members receive special terms.
For more information about the event, follow the links: https://cutt.ly/9yQmTlnY
Interfax-Ukraine is the conference’s media partner.

Drone strikes cut power across southeast Sudan, operator says
CAIRO, Oct 26 - Paramilitary drone strikes hit power stations in southeast Sudan on Monday, cutting power across the region, the state electricity company said.
The operator accused the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces — which have been fighting a civil war with the army for around 3-1/2 years — of knocking out power in four states, which cover about half the territory currently held by the military.
The Rapid Support Forces did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the account from the Sudan Electricity Holding Company.
Power was cut in Sennar, Al Qadarif, White Nile and Gezira states, threatening the stability of the whole national grid, the operator said.
The attacks hit stations in the towns and areas of Sinja, El Hawata, Al Fao and Mashkour, as well as Al-Junaid in Gezira State, causing "severe damage" and "major destruction" to equipment, it added.
The United Nations has warned that attacks on power infrastructure threaten health and other services for millions of people already hit hard by the conflict.
Sudan's army has been fighting the Rapid Support Forces since April 2023, when the two fell out over issues including how to integrate their forces in a planned transition to civilian rule.
Both sides have stepped up drone strikes, with a series of attacks on Nyala, held by the RSF, and Khartoum airport, held by the army, this month. REUTERS

Koretsky: government must deliver new mobilization social contract by Dec 1
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
13:19:28 EET
20:19:28 KST

Prime Minister of Ukraine Serhiy Koretsky predicts that following changes to the reservation system, over 90-95% of employees in the fuel-energy and defense-industrial complexes will be re-reserved.
"We are separating the concept of criticality from economic reservation criteria. This is very important. Why? Because salary and the absence of tax debt are not the same as an enterprise's criticality. This is important, it indeed brings transparency, cleanup, and additional revenues, but it does not equal criticality. Critical means energy, the defense-industrial complex, communications, housing and communal services, pharmacies, groceries, logistics, and so on. But there are enterprises, a large number already, that got there largely due to salaries and a lack of tax debts. Therefore, we are separating criticality from the economy," Koretsky said at the 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF) themed "People. Business. Economy. What's Next?" in Kyiv on Monday, as reported by an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent.
He emphasized that workers currently in the energy sector or the defense-industrial complex have nothing to worry about, as over 90-95% will be re-reserved.
"However, creating a large number of enterprises, whether IT or conditionally defense industry, where three drones are made and hundreds of people are reserved – I am conditionally simplifying, hyperbolizing in a certain sense, but that is how it is. And there are very many such cases. Contracting organizations. And it grows, grows, grows," he added.
According to the Prime Minister, changing the rules is designed, on the one hand, to cut down on unfair reservations without letting the economy collapse, and on the other hand, to give active military personnel a clear understanding regarding rotations.
"To say that these mobilization and reservation rules will produce a super-effect – no, there is no such thing, but we are at least stopping the endless growth of sometimes unfairly reserved individuals. And now, most importantly, what I am appealing to enterprises, business, and the economic sector about: we need to jointly come up with a new social model where, even if everyone is reserved, enterprises provide predictable mobilization of people into the army. This is an idealistic model. If such a solution could be found, the need to search for people on the streets would disappear. And if a business, entrepreneur, manager, or head takes on such a commitment – then nothing else is needed at all, this is a new social contract. But not thinking about it, not preparing for it, is a super-strategic mistake," Koretsky stated.
He stressed that failing to prepare in advance for a potential tightening of mobilization in Russia, which could reach 300,000–500,000 troops, would mean being forced to make unpopular decisions in manual mode once again.
"Then it won't be about reservations, or percentages. The issue is the survival of the state, and therefore this must be taken into account. Seeking to increase accountability for those who hide is also on the agenda – this is all a comprehensive story. By December 1, we must deliver a new social contract," he added, announcing a meeting with businesses on this issue.
As reported, on October 23, Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky stated that the Cabinet of Ministers had finalized changes to the reservation system – an enterprise's criticality is being separated from its economic indicators, sectoral and regional criticality criteria will be updated, and enterprises will be checked for abuses.
The second change is that the maximum reservation level, particularly for the energy sector and defense industry, will no longer be 100% (dropping to 95%). The government will not weaken the work of those manufacturing weapons or maintaining critical infrastructure, and if uninterrupted operation requires reserving more, the enterprise can submit a justified appeal to a special Coordination Center.
The third change involves the Ministry of Defense strengthening liability for draft evasion. The fourth is the preparation of a mechanism for 100% reservation provided mobilization obligations are fulfilled: an enterprise will be able to fully reserve employees if it regularly and voluntarily recruits a portion of them for military service.
The Cabinet has also initiated a review of sectoral and regional criticality criteria, taking into account new requirements within 10 days.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on October 26, 2026
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
19:16:18 CST
20:16:18 KST

At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Iceland Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir will visit China from October 26 to 31.
CCTV: China released the Progress Report on the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All at the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an). How does China see the role of AI capacity-building in global governance?
Guo Jiakun: Artificial intelligence is an emerging field in global governance, and a litmus test for the effectiveness of the global governance system. The global governance system would not become more just and equitable without the collective capacity enhancement of the Global South, and requires concrete efforts to strengthen the representation and voice of developing countries. China advocates for respecting the digital sovereignty of all countries. We believe that every country has the right to possess the foundational capabilities for independent AI development, and to seek a development path suited to its national conditions and practical needs, one that enables AI to be applied in real-world scenarios, address real problems, and generate sustained value.
As a responsible major country, China remains committed to providing global public goods in the field of AI. In 2024, China promoted the adoption of a UN General Assembly resolution on enhancing international cooperation on capacity-building of artificial intelligence, established the Group of Friends for International Cooperation on AI Capacity-Building, and released the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All. Over the past two years, China has taken major steps and practical measures to honor its commitment in advancing the above-mentioned initiative. Recently, at the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an), China released the Progress Report on the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All, which systematically reviews the cooperation outcomes, practical experience and specific cases since the Action Plan was launched two years ago. The report identifies access to technology as the starting point and independent development as the goal, stresses the importance of demand-driven approaches, joint consultation and co-development for project delivery, and calls for promoting openness and open source and advancing AI models, data, and talent in a coordinated manner.
Looking ahead, we welcome more countries to join the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, to explore more pathways for international cooperation on AI capacity-building, and to promote global AI development for good and for all with concrete actions.
Brasil de Fato: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has just won the reelection. Does the Chinese foreign ministry have a comment or message regarding the outcome of this election and the prospect of China-Brazil relations on Lula’s next term? (Similar question from UOL of Brazil)
Guo Jiakun: China takes note of the announcement by Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court of President Lula’s runoff victory and extends congratulations on that. China stands ready to work with Brazil to advance the building of the China-Brazil community with a shared future.
Asahi Shimbun: Former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda just passed away. What’s your comment?
Guo Jiakun: We express deep condolences and grief over former Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda’s passing and heartfelt sympathies to his family.
Mr. Yasuo Fukuda is an old friend of the Chinese people, who actively contributed to the improvement and development of China-Japan relations. He has long been committed to the friendship between our two countries, and held a correct view of history. During his tenure as prime minister, China and Japan signed the fourth political document. After leaving office, he visited the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre. What’s more, he served for many years as Chairman of the Boao Forum for Asia, playing an important role in facilitating exchanges and cooperation in Asia.
Mr. Yasuo Fukuda once noted that the four political documents between China and Japan stipulated the principles governing bilateral relations, which we must bear in mind and never deviate from. Those firm and important remarks reflected the honor and responsibility of Japan’s statesman of the older generation and should evoke self-reflection and soul-searching among those currently running the Japanese government.
AFP: Just following up on Brazil, Bolsonaro has called for those election results to be annulled. Does China have a comment on that?
Guo Jiakun: China respects the choice of the Brazilian people.
People’s Daily: On October 23, Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Foreign Minister Wang Yi announced at the opening ceremony of the Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an) that China would issue a Position on Strengthening Outer Space Governance. Could you offer more information?
Guo Jiakun: Outer space is the common frontier of all humanity and space exploration is humanity’s common endeavor. As announced by Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Foreign Minister Wang Yi at the opening ceremony of the Global Governance Forum (Xiong’an), China has issued its Position on Strengthening Outer Space Governance. This is a major step by China to deliver on the four major global initiatives and advance efforts in building a community with a shared future for humanity in outer space.
The position paper takes the common values of humanity as the fundamental guidance and advocates that the development and security, as well as the stability and sustainability of outer space, should be pursued in a balanced way. It proposes that we should commit to openness and shared benefit, abide by the international rule of law, respect the rights of all States, advance innovation and development, safeguard common security, prevent armed conflicts, reduce misunderstanding and misperception, regulate commercial space activity, deepen international cooperation, and promote global governance.
The position paper outlines constructive approaches to address issues of common concern including development, security and governance in outer space, and provides a blueprint for relevant discussions and formulation of rules by the international community. China will continue working together with all parties in an open and constructive spirit to ensure that the outcomes of space development better benefit all humanity.
China Daily: To follow up on Icelandic Foreign Minister Gunnarsdóttir’s upcoming visit you just announced, how does China see the current state of China-Iceland relations? What are your expectations for the visit?
Guo Jiakun: We welcome Foreign Minister Gunnarsdóttir to visit China. China-Iceland relations have enjoyed sound momentum of growth in recent years. In 2025, when President Tómasdóttir was in China for the Global Leaders’ Meeting on Women, President Xi met with her and they reached important common understandings on deepening cooperation in such areas as economy and trade, geothermal energy, and people-to-people and cultural exchanges. As we mark the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between China and Iceland this year, the Chinese side looks forward to in-depth exchanges with the Icelandic side on bilateral relations and international and regional issues of mutual interest to further enhance trust, advance cooperation and renew our friendship.
Yonhap News Agency: General Secretary of the Workers’ Party of Korea (WPK) and President of the State Affairs of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) Kim Jong Un visited Dandong, China last week. Was the visit proposed by China or the DPRK? Can you share more information on this visit?
Guo Jiakun: On October 24, Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and Chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) Wang Huning accompanied General Secretary of the WPK and President of the State Affairs of the DPRK Kim Jong Un on a visit to Dandong. Wang Huning conveyed General Secretary of the Central Committee of the CPC and President Xi Jinping’s cordial greetings and best wishes to Kim Jong Un. China released a readout, which you may refer to.
China and the DPRK are friendly neighbors. It is an unswerving strategic policy of the CPC and the Chinese government to maintain, consolidate and develop China-DPRK relations. The sound and steady development of the China-DPRK traditional friendly cooperative ties is in the interest of both peoples and conducive to regional peace, stability, development and prosperity. China stands ready to work with the DPRK to deliver on the important common understandings of the two heads of state and further advance bilateral ties.
Reuters: Regarding the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting Plus that will be held from this Wednesday in Manila, will China be participating in that meeting? Whether it’s sending high-level officials or delegation?
Guo Jiakun: The ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting Plus is meant to play a positive role in enabling regional countries to step up dialogue, increase trust and promote cooperation. We oppose attempts by anyone to use this platform to seek selfish gains, hijack ASEAN and create trouble.
AFP: The United States last week designated the Confucius Institute Cultural Centers on American universities and campuses as a threat to U.S. national security, would China like to comment?
Guo Jiakun: We reject vilification and smears against Confucius Institute. Educational exchange and cooperation between China and the U.S. help enhance mutual understanding between the peoples of the two countries. They are desired by both sides and benefit both sides and should not be held back or disrupted.
Beijing Youth Daily: Yesterday, the 25th of October, is the eighth Anti-Sanctions Day designated by the Southern African Development Community. Zimbabwe recently held commemorative events and called for the immediate removal of the illegal sanctions imposed by Western countries. What’s your comment?
Guo Jiakun: China supports Zimbabwe in commemorating the Anti-Sanctions Day.
The illegal sanctions imposed by certain Western countries on Zimbabwe have lasted for over 20 years. The practice is a typical example of hegemonism. It seriously violates Zimbabwe’s national sovereignty, undermines Zimbabwean people’s right to development, and hurts international fairness and justice. China has supported the just aspiration of Zimbabwe and other African friends in various ways for eight consecutive years. China solemnly calls on certain Western countries to immediately remove the illegal sanctions imposed on Zimbabwe, and take responsible and concrete actions to develop the economy and improve people’s livelihoods there. China will work with African countries and the rest of the world to safeguard international fairness and justice, and support Zimbabwe in defending independence and sovereignty as well as achieving development and revitalization.
AFP: Serbia’s student-led movement won parliamentary elections on Sunday, ending 14 years in power for Aleksandar Vucic’s party. I was wondering if China would comment on the fact that Vucic said that the student movement was carried out with direct support from various European countries and the U.S. deep state.
Guo Jiakun: China upholds the principle of non-interference in internal affairs and respects the independent choice of the people of other countries.
We attach great importance to China-Serbia relations and stand ready to work with Serbia’s new government to carry forward our traditional friendship, consolidate political mutual trust and expand practical cooperation on the basis of mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, so as to maintain the steady and sustained growth of bilateral ties.
Bloomberg: India has held the Chinese military responsible for disturbing the peace on the border amid reports of fresh confrontation. A spokesman from India’s ministry of external affairs said this happens when Chinese forces diverge from established patterns. Does the foreign ministry have any comment?
Guo Jiakun: China strictly abides by the relevant agreements and common understandings reached between the two countries, and conducts normal border patrol and control activities to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and stability in the border areas. China and India maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels. We hope that India will work with China in the same direction by jointly implementing the common understandings reached between the two sides and maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas with concrete actions.

Spanish low-cost airline Volotea has canceled more than 10% of its winter flight capacity in France amid soaring jet fuel prices and mounting financial pressures, leaving passengers scrambling for alternatives, according to a report Monday.
The carrier, which operates many domestic routes in France and connects medium-sized European cities, is struggling with rising kerosene costs and €250-300 million ($280-336 million) of debt accumulated during the COVID-19 pandemic, BFMTV reported.
Consumer association UFC Que Choisir criticized the airline's handling of cancellations, citing passenger complaints about delayed refunds and inadequate assistance with alternative travel arrangements.
Under EU regulations, airlines must offer passengers either refunds within seven days or alternative transportation when flights are canceled.
Volotea said refunds were being processed within seven days, while reimbursement requests for alternative travel expenses would be assessed individually.
According to aviation analytics firm Cirium, the airline has eliminated over 10% of its capacity between November and February.
Bordeaux has reportedly experienced the sharpest reductions, with cancellations reaching 35% year-on-year.
Volotea also plans to reduce its fleet from 44 aircraft to approximately 30-35, focusing on larger planes to improve revenue per seat.

Ukrainian who fled Oleshky views US-brokered ceasefire with deep scepticism
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
11:15:51 UTC
20:15:51 KST

Ukrainian who fled Oleshky views US-brokered ceasefire with deep scepticism
KYIV, Oct 26 - Six weeks ago, Vitaly, his wife Iryna, their 13-year-old son Vlad and their cat left the besieged town of Oleshky in Russian-occupied Ukraine to escape what they feared was certain death by starvation.
Now back in Ukraine after a gruelling journey via Russia and Belarus, Vitaly views with deep scepticism a temporary ceasefire in his native town set to begin on Tuesday to allow evacuations and send in supplies.
Russia and Ukraine reached the agreement, announced by the White House on Friday, with the mediation of US first lady Melania Trump and after additional involvement from Pope Leo.
After more than four years living under Russian occupation in a town on the front line of fierce fighting with Ukrainian forces, Vitaly is not optimistic that the ceasefire can hold for long or the humanitarian situation significantly improve.
"Regarding the truce, I'm very sceptical about all this," said Vitaly, 55, who declined to give his last name for security reasons because his relatives were still living in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine.
"I have a lot of respect for Melania Trump, but she does not influence dictator (Russian President Vladimir) Putin," he told Reuters, sitting in a modern apartment in the Kyiv region where his family has temporarily settled.
He said many of those remaining in Oleshky are sick or elderly and it would be difficult for them to relocate.
Ukraine and Russia blame each other for the humanitarian crisis in Oleshky. Drones present the greatest threat to civilian life, and the town is within easy reach of unmanned aerial vehicles belonging to both armies.
Because supplies are running out and the route north is blocked by the Dnipro river, some residents have walked 20 km (12 miles) to the next village to stock up on food and water. The journey is fraught with danger and locals call it the "road of death".
TEMPORARY CEASEFIRE AGREED
Ukraine and Russia agreed to a temporary ceasefire around Oleshky that is expected to begin on October 27 at 3 a.m. Kyiv time (0100 GMT).
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that Kyiv hoped it would be possible to open up Oleshky, provide access for food and medicine and allow people to leave the area.
The Kremlin has said that all civilians wishing to leave Oleshky would be allowed to do so and that the evacuation was expected to take at least several days.
Oleshky, a small town across the Dnipro from Ukraine's regional hub of Kherson, had a prewar population of some 24,000. It is still home to around 1,700 residents, including about 35 children, according to the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine.
UNDER RUSSIAN CONTROL
Russian troops have occupied Oleshky since the first days of the full-scale invasion in February 2022.
It has been largely cut off from running water, electricity, gas and central heating since the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam in 2023 and subsequent flooding of nearby areas.
As the war ground on, the humanitarian crisis deepened. By the middle of last year, the constant threat of drones choked off supply lines, causing food scarcity.
And from late May this year, the situation became severe, according to residents Reuters has spoken to.
Vitaly said his family survived for weeks by rationing a single cup of rice or buckwheat a day, occasionally adding a cucumber or tomato mixed with purslane, a common wild weed.
During the summer months, some residents could sell vegetables, but prices were unaffordable for most.
A kilo of tomatoes cost about 1,500 roubles ($18.50). To buy eggs, you needed to know the right people and 10 eggs would cost around 3,000 roubles, Vitaly recalled. No one was willing to sell potatoes.
After counting their meagre food stocks, and remembering last winter when the temperature in their apartment dropped to between 1 and 3 degrees Celsius (34 and 37 degrees Fahrenheit), they decided to leave.
"You look at what remained from your food supplies and realize that there is only one way for you — to go on foot or die of hunger," Vitaly said.
Their home in Oleshky had been damaged by a drone, Iryna said, and they did not have anything left there.
ARDUOUS ESCAPE
On September 13, the family joined a small party of eight people and set out on foot. They walked for more than 20 km to the village of Radensk.
The road was heavily mined, and drones were flying overhead. Vitaly said they saw the body of a woman lying on the road as they passed by. They took with them only their autumn clothes, Vlad's teddy bear, the cat and a handful of family photos.
They travelled from Radensk by bus deeper into Russian-occupied Ukraine, crossed into Russia after lengthy questioning by authorities at the border, and finally Belarus before returning to Ukrainian-controlled territory on September 17.
The family has spent the past several weeks settling into a new routine in the Kyiv region.
One of their first purchases was a bag of potatoes, bought to cook mashed potatoes for their son.
"The kid will be in school. We will be working. My wife needs to get her health back on track a bit," Vitaly said.
As for his own future: "I will either join the army or will try to find a position somewhere here with weapon producers to help our country defeat its enemies." REUTERS

Japanese company to compensate users hit by cyberattack
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
11:52:50 UTC
20:52:50 KST

GMO Internet, a Japanese internet infrastructure company, will compensate customers for losses from unauthorised trading linked to a cyberattack on its cloud service, and will make a ¥5,000 (€28) goodwill payment to every customer currently using the affected service.
A Japanese internet infrastructure company is compensating customers affected by unauthorised transactions following a cyberattack on its cloud service.
GMO Internet announced on Saturday that it would cover losses from unauthorised trading linked to the attack and issue a ¥5,000 (€28) goodwill payment to all customers currently using the affected service, regardless of whether they had suffered financial losses.
The attack targeted Onamae.com Desktop Cloud, a virtual private server service used by customers to access remote desktop environments. GMO said customer information had been taken and some users had reported transactions in their trading accounts they did not recognise.
According to the company’s founder and CEO, Masatoshi Kumagai, the incident potentially affected 26,739 servers and involved unauthorised operations on trading accounts held with more than 70 securities and foreign-exchange firms in Japan and overseas.
GMO shares fell almost 16% on Monday to a four-month low. The company had a market value of around $2.6 billion at Friday’s close.
The company began investigating on 19 October after receiving a customer inquiry. It confirmed the installation of a malicious programme on some customer server environments on 20 October, suspended new applications and access to the service’s control panel, and began shutting down all servers the following day to prevent further damage.
In a blog post on Sunday, Kumagai apologised for the company’s response and acknowledged that security issues had been identified by its security specialists before the incident, but that the response had been insufficient.
GMO said it had received a ransom demand from a party believed to be behind the attack. In an update to his blog post on Monday, Kumagai said the attackers had demanded $50 million in cryptocurrency and threatened to disclose company and customer information. The company has refused to pay and is cooperating with the police and other authorities.
GMO will offer customers who wish to continue using a Windows desktop environment an alternative service on independent cloud infrastructure, free for six months. It also plans to overhaul its security architecture and investigate the cause of the breach with external experts.
Kumagai has urged the Japanese government to strengthen its active cyberdefence measures, arguing that private companies cannot tackle sophisticated cross-border cyberattacks alone.
GMO has asked the authorities to consider applying the framework to the incident and has offered to share evidence and technical information with investigators.
The attack comes amid wider concerns over cybersecurity following the disclosure last week of two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language widely used to build websites and applications.
Security authorities warned that the flaws could allow attackers to execute malicious code on vulnerable servers, prompting organisations around the world to patch systems or temporarily take services offline.
However, GMO has not publicly confirmed a link between the PHP vulnerabilities and the attack on its cloud service.
Separately, a Google Cloud outage in the UK disrupted online services last week, including those operated by financial technology company Revolut, showing the potential knock-on effects when digital infrastructure fails.

Frozen Russian assets key to covering Ukraine's 2027 financing needs – National Bank governor
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
13:13:04 EET
20:13:04 KST

The issue of immobilized Russian assets is being discussed in the context of the need to find confirmed sources of financing to cover the "gap" in the state budget for 2027, which Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky estimated at $32.6 billion at the Ukraine Ministerial Roundtable on October 14 during the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) Governor Andriy Pyshnyy said.
"Currently, the IMF chief [Kristalina Georgieva] has confirmed the need for assurances from partners regarding coverage of this 'gap,' which has been verified by the IMF. The IMF is also considering, in this context, the use of immobilized assets in a way that European partners would consider acceptable to them, in order to ensure that Ukraine receives the necessary amount of financing," Pyshnyy said in an interview with Interfax-Ukraine on the sidelines of the Annual Meetings.
According to him, the IMF always discusses this issue very cautiously, recognizing that its mandate and influence are limited.
"But the IMF is involved in discussions on the format for accessing immobilized assets. For example, the Fund may recommend paying attention to a factor such as debt sustainability, so that the use of immobilized assets does not create additional interest-rate pressure for Ukraine. As for how exactly this will be structured, that will be determined by the European bureaucracy," the NBU governor explained.
He said he was optimistic about the possibility of continuing to use immobilized Russian assets to finance Ukraine and mentioned the evolution of the IMF's and the European Central Bank's positions on the issue.
"This issue requires complex, comprehensive communication on the part of the president, the government and the National Bank. You have seen how many meetings I have had here: over these past few days, I have held dozens of discussions with partners. This issue remains one of our priorities," Pyshnyy said.
As reported, in 2024, the G7 established the Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration (ERA) mechanism, providing Ukraine with $50 billion in unconditional, non-repayable financing based on discounting future cash flows from the further investment of Russian assets immobilized in Europe, primarily at Euroclear, totaling approximately EUR 200 billion. Most of the $50 billion is scheduled to be disbursed in 2025–2026, while only $1.4 billion is allocated for 2027.
In addition, after the idea of a EUR 140 billion reparations loan for the EU backed by the same proceeds from frozen Russian assets fell through in autumn 2025, the EU developed the Ukraine Support Loan (USL), a EUR 90 billion mechanism for 2026–2027 to provide military and nonmilitary support to Ukraine. This is also non-repayable assistance to Ukraine; however, the allocation of part of the funding for budget financing is tied to Kyiv's fulfillment of reform conditions.
The 2027 state budget currently provides for $52.6 billion in external financing, of which only approximately $20 billion comes from confirmed sources. In mid-October, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, taking defense spending into account, estimated Ukraine's total additional financing needs for 2027 at EUR 70 billion while in Brussels.
As part of efforts to secure these funds, according to available information, consideration is being given to launching ERA-2 and/or USL-2 mechanisms by continuing to discount future cash flows from Russian Federation assets immobilized for a longer period or investing them in higher-yielding assets.

Trump officials back Orbán bid for UN secretary-general, WSJ reports
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
11:11:58 UTC
20:11:58 KST

The WSJ reports that Trump administration officials are floating former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán for UN secretary-general, potentially backed by the US, Russia and China, though nothing is confirmed and his selection remains uncertain.
Officials in the Trump administration are advocating the nomination of former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán for the post of UN secretary-general, according to a report by the Wall Street Journal.
The newspaper reports that Orbán could be a joint American, Russian and Chinese candidate, and that sources in all three countries have confirmed the Trump administration is backing his bid.
Orbán lost power in Hungary’s parliamentary election in April, when Péter Magyar’s Tisza party defeated him after 16 years of governing with an absolute majority.
His hard-right, fiercely anti-migration and eurosceptic policies, together with the rule of law backsliding in Hungary, strained relations with Western allies, including the European Union and NATO. Nevertheless, Orbán maintained close ties with Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Since the election, Hungarian authorities have launched fraud and corruption investigations into several members of Orbán’s former government. Two former ministers and the former governor of Hungary’s National Bank are under arrest, and authorities could also examine Orbán’s potential involvement in those cases.
According to the WSJ, no final decision has been taken on the plan. A US State Department official admitted that the idea sounds crazy at first, but said previous talks with Washington suggest Russia and China also support it. The aim is for Orbán to be the joint candidate of the three countries.
“If the United States, Russia and China want the same thing in the UN Security Council, they usually achieve it,” officials from the United States and another country told the newspaper. The second five-year term of the current secretary-general, António Guterres, ends on 31 December.
The White House, Moscow and Beijing have not confirmed the information.
Euronews has contacted Orbán’s spokesperson for comment but has not yet received a response. The spokesperson previously dismissed press reports about Orbán’s candidacy for the post of deputy secretary-general as “fake news”.
In May, the VSquare investigative newsletter reported that a UN position could be important for the former prime minister because of the diplomatic immunity attached to the role.
According to the WSJ, Orbán would only run if his victory were assured, a scenario that currently seems unlikely. A candidate must secure the support of at least nine of the 15 Security Council members, while any of the five permanent members can veto the nomination. Besides the US, Russia and China, France and the United Kingdom are also permanent members.

Israel, but not in Palestine?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
11:11:49 UTC
20:11:49 KST

Argentina, 1896
In ‘The Jewish State’, Theodor Herzl, the founder of political Zionism, proposed Palestine and Argentina as possible locations for a Jewish state, citing Argentina’s fertile land and Palestine’s historical significance to Jews.
Cyprus, 1901–1902
Herzl and other Zionist leaders explored establishing a Jewish settlement in then British-controlled Cyprus, but the idea never became an approved proposal.
Egypt’s Sinai Peninsula, 1902–1903
Herzl negotiated with British authorities to establish a settlement near El Arish. The plan depended on Nile water but failed to win Egyptian approval.
British East Africa, 1903
British Colonial Secretary Joseph Chamberlain proposed territory in present-day Kenya. The Zionist Congress agreed to study the “Uganda Scheme”, but rejected it in 1905 after fierce divisions.
Angola, 1907–1913
The Jewish Territorialist Organisation, led by Israel Zangwill, explored alternatives to Palestine. Angola, then a Portuguese colony, was considered but the plan never materialised.
Palestine, 1947
UN Resolution 181 proposed dividing then British-ruled Palestine into Arab and Jewish states, with Jerusalem under international administration. Zionist leaders accepted the plan, while Palestinian Arab leaders and Arab states rejected it. Israel was declared a state in 1948.

Russia will not slow its offensive against Ukraine despite plans to resume US-brokered peace talks, but Moscow is open to localized humanitarian ceasefires, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Monday.

His remarks come ahead of a localized ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky in the Kherson region, intended to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and civilian evacuations.
The agreement, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, is scheduled to take effect on Oct. 29, according to the White House. Russian and Ukrainian officials are coordinating the operation.
However, Peskov made clear that the arrangement would not signal a broader halt to Russia’s war against Ukraine.
“The decision to resume trilateral talks does not imply any restrictions on combat operations,” he said.
“Our armed forces continue to carry out massive strikes on Ukraine’s military-industrial complex,” he added.
Oleshky сeasefire aims to evacuate civilians
Oleshky, a Russian-occupied city on the left bank of the Dnipro River opposite Kherson, has faced a worsening humanitarian crisis, with residents reporting severe shortages of food, clean water and medicine.
Before Russia’s full-scale invasion, the city had a population of about 24,000. The White House estimates that between 1,700 and 2,000 people remain, including elderly residents and around 50 children.
Bulgarian Presidential Election Exposes Split Over Ukraine War
The temporary truce is intended to allow humanitarian supplies into the city and establish a safe passage for civilians who want to leave. Residents will be able to choose whether to evacuate to Ukrainian-controlled territory or Russia, according to the White House.
Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets, who led Kyiv’s negotiating team, confirmed the agreement and said the operation would be implemented in stages.
Melania Trump said she worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian representatives to coordinate the arrangement. Her involvement builds on previous efforts to reunite Ukrainian children separated from their families during Russia’s war.
Russia intensifies attacks as talks approach
The latest diplomatic push follows meetings between US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21.
The envoys had held consultations with Ukrainian and European officials in Oslo the previous day.
On Sunday, Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said Moscow was ready to resume trilateral negotiations with Ukraine and the US after Nov. 4, following Russia’s National Unity Day holiday.
“After that, we will be ready to resume negotiations,” Ushakov said, according to Russian state media.
He cautioned against expecting an immediate breakthrough, describing the next round as an opportunity to explore the parties’ positions rather than reach a final agreement.
Working-level delegations could meet in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland to prepare for further discussions.
Previous rounds of negotiations have failed to bring the sides closer to a settlement. Moscow continues to demand additional Ukrainian territory and sweeping restrictions on Kyiv’s military and political independence.
Ukraine and its allies have rejected those demands as unacceptable, warning that concessions imposed under pressure could leave the country vulnerable to another Russian attack.

International parcels drop by 32% after EU imposes surcharge
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
The number of parcels sent from outside the Netherlands dropped by one-third in the last three months, mainly as a result of tighter EU restrictions, postal service PostNL said in its latest quarterly report.
The company said the 32% drop mainly reflected a drop in packages being sent from Asia after the EU imposed a €3 surcharge per product on July 1.
It follows a 15% dip in the second quarter of the year and PostNL expects the trend to continue after the import fees are raised by a further €2 from next month.
The impact was partly offset by a 40% increase in parcels within the EU last year as Asian websites lost trade to European rivals as a result of the new measures.
But PostNL said that growth was “more than wiped out” by the drop in deliveries from further afield.
Three-day deliveries
The company’s turnover increased in the third quarter by €6 million to €786 million after the government relaxed the rules on deliveries.
Since July PostNL has been required to deliver letters within two days rather than 24 hours and the deadline is due to be stretched to three days next July.
CEO Pim Berendsen said the move to three-day deliveries was an essential “interim step” towards ensuring the postal service could survive in the long term, but also renewed his calls for the government to compensate the company’s losses in recent years.
“Until we have a future-proofed regulatory framework, the uncertainty for thousands of our postal workers, customers and consumers will continue,” he said. “This situation requires a structural solution.”

Sudan Electricity Holding Company said Monday that drone attacks by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) targeted five power substations, causing extensive damage and a complete blackout across the country’s southeast.
In a statement, the company said the strikes targeted substations in Singa, Al-Hawata, Al-Faw, Mashkur and Al-Junaid in central and southeastern Sudan.
“The attacks caused significant damage to components of the facilities and completely cut electricity from the southeastern grid, affecting Sennar, Gedaref, White Nile and Gezira states,” said the statement cited by local media.
It warned that the damage also threatened the stability of Sudan’s national electricity grid.
“Engineering and technical teams were dispatched to the affected substations to assess the damage and begin repairs aimed at restoring electricity and stabilizing the grid as soon as possible,” it added.
The daily Sudan Tribune said an RSF drone struck the Al-Junaid power substation in eastern Gezira state early Monday, knocking it out of service and cutting electricity to the area.
The outlet said RSF drones also attempted to strike strategic fuel depots in Umm Aliyla in eastern Gezira without causing damage. The facility had been targeted in September, when a drone attack sparked a fire at one of its storage units.
In Sennar, the state government said an RSF drone struck the Singa power substation, causing material damage and injuring members of the facility’s guard team.
Drones also targeted the Al-Faw and Al-Hawata substations in Gedaref state, cutting electricity supplies, while another drone struck the Mashkur substation in White Nile state, causing a local power outage.
The RSF has intensified drone attacks in recent days against fuel storage facilities and electricity infrastructure in North Kordofan, Gedaref, Gezira and White Nile states amid escalating fighting with army forces.
The army and the RSF have been at war since April 2023 following disputes over integrating the paramilitary group into the military. The conflict has killed tens of thousands and displaced around 13 million people, fueling one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.

Unknown Publisher
2026-10-26
11:09:13 UTC
20:09:13 KST

About 90,000 properties across northern parts of the UK are still without power after a weekend of stormy weather, with forecasters warning of more strong winds to come.
Two men were killed by falling trees after two named storms, Austen and Boelo, pummelled parts of the UK, bringing widespread travel disruption, flooding, power cuts and event cancellations.
On Monday morning, the Energy Networks Association, which represents operators in the UK and Ireland, said 90,000 customers were still without power.
The association’s chief executive, Lawrence Slade, told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme that disruption had been widespread with operators having to restore power to about 700,000 customers over the weekend.
He said Friday, Saturday and Sunday had been particularly challenging. “It certainly was a tough one. One of the problems was how quickly Boelo followed after Austen.”
Another issue was that there was no letup in the strong winds, widely 50-70mph and up to 85mph in northern Scotland. “Until that weather system passes we can’t safely get engineers out to replace poles, to get wires back up etc.”
The weather was much milder on Monday but the Met Office said more strong winds were on the way and issued two yellow weather warnings. One is in place from 6pm until 3am on Tuesday, covering western coastal areas from Cornwall up to south-west Scotland. Gusts of up to 65mph could hit exposed coastal areas, accompanied by heavy rain at times. The Met Office warned people to take care near cliffs and be aware of strong waves.
The second warning is in place from 3am to 9pm on Tuesday and covers most of Scotland. Forecasters said winds of 50-60mph were likely to be quite widespread with gusts up to 70mph in the far north. It warned of possible travel cancellations, road closures and more power cuts.
The weekend storms led to two deaths, authorities said. A 60-year-old man was hit by a falling tree in Dumfries and Galloway while a man in his 20s died in Finchley, north London.
Scotland’s first minister, John Swinney, met senior politicians, emergency teams and forecasters on Sunday to discuss the ongoing response to the weather, amid the warnings of more to come.
On Monday, Swinney posted on X: “My deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the two people who have tragically lost their lives as a result of Storm Boelo. My thoughts are with all those affected by the damage and I thank the emergency services working through the night to keep people safe.”
There were also pockets of flooding with dramatic footage from Largs town centre showing flood water cascading through the town centre. One resident said it was the highest she had ever seen in 36 years of living there. Staff at the Thai restaurant Tha-Tien-Thai shared a video of their kitchen overrun by water with the desperate caption: “There is nothing left.” They said its doors would be closed for the foreseeable future “due to larger flood restoration than originally planned”.
Emergency services were called to a flooded care home in Saltcoats, North Ayrshire, on Sunday evening. Police Scotland said everyone at the care home was accounted for, road closures were in place and officers were expected to remain on site overnight to assist.
There was also travel disruption, with being flights diverted from landing at Leeds Bradford, England’s highest airport, and others cancelled. Most train services were getting back to normal although operators advised customers to check before they travelled.
The storms brought a number of event cancellations including the Sunday racing at Aintree, abandoned because of the high winds. The Guardian’s live blog of the tea-time Sunderland v Leeds goalless draw summed up the action: “And the winner is … the wind.”
